data.name: Robo Do It
data.detailed_description:
Robo Do It is a funny game (made in México) to learn logic programming without writing code by building scripts to program robots in each level. The goal is to find the best solution to create an algorithm that takes these robots into victory capsules.

In this videogame, the player is introduced into a 3d world filled with levels where the main objective is to help one or more robots to reach the capsules by assigning commands or actions (such as to forward, to turn, to jump, and others) that are logically programmable and iconographic, the latter to facilitate the understanding and learning of the player. On the other hand, with the passage of levels, the difficulty of the game increases, challenging the player with new challenges that encompass the sequential, repetitive and conditional control structures of programming in general, as well as inciting the player to apply the reuse and reduction of commands that are equivalent to the real programming code.

Robo Do It have two game modes, the game arcade and the level editor. In the game arcade you need to solve forty eight levels along four chapters and in the level editor you will use your skills to create a great, funny and complex level what you can test and share with players community. Also you can follow, download, play, get score and rate like bad or nice level from another players levels!

Get the best score by collecting all gems in game, getting a better time and using less commands to reach de victory!

Features:
  • Infinite possibilities of gameplay thanks to the level creator and the community.
  • This game help people to learn programming logic by a very funny and easy way.
  • 32 arcade levels with many hours of fun (and 12 arcade levels are comming) and all the levels created by the community for free.
  • Level editor to create, share, follow, download, play, rate and solve many levels from another players and getting the best score!
  • Each level game can have gems, robots, blocks, buttons, doors, mobile platforms and victory capsules in differents floors!
  • You can play offline and be syncronized when you log in with your steam account.
  • Different robot commands to do many actions like walk, turn, jump, climb, use mechanisms, conditionals, procedures and more!
  • In level editor you can place objects wherever you want in a grid map with fourth floors, they can be configured and have an interesting objetive.
  • Use your steam account to join automatically in robo do it!
  • Ranking for best players
  • Social Chat for players whom are in Robo Do it

reviews.review:
Robo Do It is a puzzle-driven programming game developed by Angel Carriola and published by Glossware Studios and Dosane Games. Designed to teach logical thinking and fundamental coding concepts through interactive challenges, the game successfully bridges the gap between education and entertainment. Instead of overwhelming players with complex programming languages or technical terminology, it introduces computational thinking through accessible visual commands and engaging puzzle design. The result is a title that manages to be both a useful learning tool and a genuinely enjoyable puzzle experience.

The game's central concept revolves around controlling robots indirectly through programmed instructions. Rather than moving characters manually, players create sequences of commands that determine how robots behave within various environments. These commands include movement, turning, jumping, interacting with objects, and eventually more advanced logical operations. Once a sequence is prepared, the robot executes the instructions exactly as programmed, allowing players to observe the outcome and identify mistakes. This process mirrors the real-world principles of programming while remaining approachable enough for players of all ages.

One of the most impressive aspects of Robo Do It is how naturally it introduces increasingly advanced concepts. Early puzzles focus on simple movement and navigation, helping players become comfortable with the interface and core mechanics. As the game progresses, more sophisticated tools become available, including loops, reusable functions, conditional actions, and optimization challenges. Each new mechanic builds logically upon previous lessons, creating a smooth learning curve that rarely feels overwhelming.

The puzzle design is consistently thoughtful and rewarding. Every level presents a specific problem that requires careful planning and analysis. Players must examine the environment, identify potential obstacles, and construct an efficient set of instructions capable of achieving the objective. Because solutions often require multiple attempts and refinements, completing a difficult puzzle creates a strong sense of satisfaction. The game excels at making players feel clever without resorting to unfair or overly obscure challenges.

A major strength of Robo Do It is its visual programming system. Instead of forcing players to learn syntax, the game uses icons and graphical commands that represent different actions and logical structures. This approach makes the experience highly accessible, especially for younger audiences and newcomers to programming. At the same time, the underlying concepts remain authentic enough to provide a meaningful introduction to coding fundamentals. Players learn how algorithms function, how repetition can simplify solutions, and how planning ahead can improve efficiency.

The progression system encourages more than simply reaching the goal. Many levels contain optional objectives such as collecting gems, reducing the number of commands used, or completing puzzles with greater efficiency. These additional goals add depth and replay value by encouraging players to revisit stages and improve their solutions. This emphasis on optimization reflects real programming practices, where elegant and efficient code is often valued as highly as functionality.

The game's campaign offers a substantial amount of content. Spread across numerous stages and chapters, the experience gradually expands its complexity while continually introducing new environmental mechanics and challenges. Players encounter moving platforms, switches, doors, elevation changes, and increasingly intricate puzzle layouts that require creative problem-solving. This variety helps maintain interest and ensures that the gameplay remains engaging throughout the adventure.

Perhaps the most valuable feature beyond the main campaign is the level editor. The inclusion of a robust creation tool allows players to design and share their own puzzles with the community. This dramatically extends the game's longevity by providing an endless source of new content. The editor encourages creativity and allows advanced players to experiment with their own puzzle ideas while giving newcomers access to community-generated challenges that go beyond the official levels.

Visually, Robo Do It favors clarity and functionality over spectacle. The environments are colorful and easy to read, ensuring that players can quickly identify important objects and understand how different elements interact. The robots themselves are charmingly designed, and the overall presentation maintains a playful tone that helps make the educational aspects feel less intimidating. While the graphics are relatively simple, they effectively support the gameplay and make the puzzles easy to understand.

The user interface deserves recognition for handling increasingly complex mechanics without becoming confusing. As new commands and systems are introduced, menus remain organized and intuitive. Players can easily edit instructions, test solutions, and analyze their mistakes. This accessibility is particularly important in a game focused on learning, and Robo Do It succeeds in making experimentation feel natural rather than frustrating.

The educational value is arguably the game's greatest achievement. Many educational games struggle to remain entertaining once their lessons become apparent, but Robo Do It avoids this pitfall by ensuring that the puzzles themselves remain enjoyable. Players learn concepts such as sequencing, optimization, problem decomposition, and logical reasoning through gameplay rather than direct instruction. The result is a learning experience that feels rewarding instead of mandatory.

The game's main limitation is that its appeal will naturally be strongest among players who enjoy puzzle-solving and logical challenges. Those looking for action, narrative-driven adventures, or fast-paced gameplay may find the experience too methodical. Some of the later puzzles can also become quite demanding, requiring patience and persistence to solve. However, these challenges are an intentional part of the game's design and contribute to the satisfaction of mastering its systems.

Overall, Robo Do It succeeds as both an entertaining puzzle game and a practical introduction to programming concepts. Through clever level design, accessible mechanics, meaningful progression, and a strong emphasis on creativity, it offers an experience that remains engaging from beginning to end. Whether approached as an educational tool or simply as a unique logic-based adventure, the game demonstrates that learning and entertainment can work together remarkably well when supported by thoughtful design.

Rating: 7/10
